context: Precedent in established schemes. Kyber [34] and Scloud+ [36] adopt analogous independence assumptions when estimating their failure rates, treating rounding errors as i.i.d. and independent of other terms (see also section 2.3 in [29]). We stress that fully eliminating the independence assumption for highdimensional lattice codes remains an open problem [33], and contemporary schemes such as NEV and DAWN rely on the same assumption. Under these circumstances, adopting the independence assumption is both a pragmatic necessity and a well-motivated choice. Under the independence assumption, the failure probability calculation reduces to computing the tail probability of a chi-squared distribution.
